status_vocabulary.met_bounded: The exact local fixture demonstrated the stated outcome only within its recorded boundary.
status_vocabulary.partial: The fixture demonstrated a necessary mechanism but did not close the whole requirement.
status_vocabulary.not_met: The evaluated composition did not demonstrate the required outcome.
status_vocabulary.not_evaluated: This corpus did not test the requirement.
status_vocabulary.preference_partial: The evidence informs a Should or optional outcome without claiming final satisfaction.

cells.scope: The carrier and relay were treated as observable and untrusted; the exact carrier files exposed neither payload nor protected forwarding-field marker, and an outsider key failed to open the member envelope.

Stable item IDs made one repeated batch harmless across a full process restart and one repeated item harmless across a membership-generation change; no complete at-least-once delivery system was tested.
Possession of a fixture member key controlled metadata visibility, but the corpus did not execute mutual peer authentication or bind carrier identity to mission identity.

The same source/member protected object was independent of the file-like carrier; BVB-808 separately demonstrates byte-identical opaque p2panda carriage, but this corpus did not rerun a physical carrier.
AES-256-GCM authenticated the member and content layers and both source signatures authenticated the encrypted source object without trusting the carrier.
The consumer and relay verified exact ES256 and ML-DSA-65 source signatures without using a carrier identity as source authority.
Three exact Event-like items were encrypted in source-created AES-256-GCM batches before carrier serialization.
Each accepted item was inside a source-created encrypted batch covered by both mandatory signature slots and a stable item ID.
The consumer verified both source signatures, authenticated both encryption layers, and only then decrypted and durably accepted the exact item IDs.
Relay B verified the source object, persisted the exact opaque carrier, fully exited, restarted, and forwarded byte-identically with no content key and zero durable-state plaintext-marker matches.
No cross-scope bridge or rewrapping policy ran.
Scope, topic, priority, route, generation, and object ID were inside a member-keyed COSE_Encrypt layer; their exact markers did not occur in the UTF-8 carrier fixture.
An exact provisioned relay member key opened the outer layer and exposed only the forwarding fields and still-encrypted source object needed by the fixture.
The outsider probe could parse the carrier wrapper but could not authenticate or decrypt the protected member envelope.

The task-authored carrier wrapper exposed a version marker, object length, nonce, and ciphertext; no packet capture or per-carrier leakage profile established that this is the minimum for every transport.
The fixture used named publisher and role identities but did not prove unique node identity issuance, cloning behavior, or carrier binding.
Keys were provisioned before child-process execution, but no mission provisioning format, trust root, or recovery workflow ran.
The fixture used pre-placed member and consumer keys; it did not prove long-term-key lifecycle or derivation.
No per-mission key derivation profile ran.
No per-scope derivation from a long-term root ran.
The exact consumer scope keys were required to read the protected batch and the relay lacked the content key; only one scope was exercised.
The relay's mesh membership key did not grant payload read access, but the corpus did not test multiple scopes or a general no-universal-read policy.

A dual-signed control object traversed the temporal relay, advanced accepted state from generation one to two, and named relay B as removed. The fixture did not distribute the new key or bind the control to OpenMLS authority state.

After accepted generation change, the replacement relay opened the generation-two envelope and the removed relay did not. Generation-two keys were directly preprovisioned, so in-field key establishment and distribution remain unproved.

A defined application hook zeroed its owned buffer, removed its logical key path, and rejected later use. Provider/HSM destruction, physical-media erasure, crash copies, and snapshot copies were explicitly not proved.

A durable acceptance journal rejected two duplicate item effects after full restart, one repeated item across generation change, and one stale generation-one batch. Restoring a pre-accept storage snapshot caused two items to be accepted again and is separately characterized as unmitigated.

The fixture selected AES-256-GCM, SHA-256/HKDF, P-256 ECDSA/ECDH, ML-DSA-65, and ML-KEM-768 from registered standardized families; the task-authored combined profile is not itself a published standard.

P-256 ECDH and ML-KEM-768 both contributed to an HKDF-SHA-256 key-confirmation fixture and four missing/tampered/downgrade negatives failed. The combiner is research scaffolding, not an adopted published hybrid profile or key-distribution mechanism.

The exact source object required ES256 and ML-DSA-65 signature slots; missing, duplicate, tampered, and authenticated-field substitution cases failed. The private profile and vectors have no independent implementation.
The executed aws-lc-rs 1.18.0 graph was explicitly non-FIPS and receives no CMVP credit.
The selected algorithms map to registered NIST/FIPS algorithm standards, but no operation-by-operation approved-mode/provider/OE matrix ran and the module was nonvalidated.
The fixed profile version and suite were authenticated, but no offer/selection negotiation, mixed-version behavior, or deprecation lifecycle ran.

The fixed object failed closed on missing/duplicate signature slots and authenticated forwarding substitution, and the hybrid-key fixture rejected missing-component and changed-suite confirmation. No negotiation or stored-policy rollback mechanism ran.
Two items shared one encrypted mandatory-both source object, demonstrating the allowed shape of batch amortization without establishing an optimal policy.
Omission, reorder, substitution, and cross-batch splice attempts all invalidated the retained source signatures; stable item IDs were durably accepted independently.
Both items remained inside the source-created authenticated ciphertext and were decrypted only by the consumer fixture.
Observed carrier sizes of 8,185 and 8,189 bytes are decision data only; no link-rate, loss, MTU, batch-size, CPU, or memory curve ran.
All cryptographic primitive operations in the fixture used exact aws-lc-rs APIs; task-authored code supplied only composition, encoding policy, durable state, and test orchestration.
coset and aws-lc-rs are exact maintained FOSS candidates, but production dependency, audit, target, side-channel, and transitive-admission gates remain open.

The awareness-bounded generation gate and old-relay key exclusion passed, while actual OpenMLS control integration, authority policy, in-field key distribution, mutual authentication, and further-exchange exclusion remain open.
Exact file-carrier and relay durable-state scans found no payload or protected forwarding markers, but no external packet capture over IP, BTLE, BP, or another physical carrier ran.

snapshot_rollback.production_disposition: unmitigated assurance and operational risk; do not silently count ordinary replay-state durability as rollback resistance
